titleText.es: En realidad no aterrizamos sobre la Luna. Sólo pareció que lo hicimos por la precesión. Además, los giroscopios provocaron el 11S.
titleText.en: We didn't actually land on the moon -- it just looked like we did because of precession.  Also, gyroscopes caused 9/11.
titleText.noteEn: The title text turns the gyroscope's real precession into two deliberately absurd conspiracy claims.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a pesar de, ‘despite’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Inside a pesar de, a is a fixed part of the connector rather than a separately translated direction word.

example.es: Salimos a pesar de la lluvia.
example.en: We went out despite the rain.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; middle of a pesar de, ‘despite’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pesar normally relates to weight or regret, but inside a pesar de the three words form one connector meaning ‘despite’ or ‘in spite of.’

example.es: Salimos a pesar de la lluvia.
example.en: We went out despite the rain.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes a pesar de, ‘despite’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De completes a pesar de and links the connector to the situation, thing, or action that did not prevent the result.

example.es: Salimos a pesar de la lluvia.
example.en: We went out despite the rain.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Encontrar can mean judging a person or thing to have a quality, not only locating something that was lost. A following describing word states that judgment.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks the personified target being judged
cardDefinitions.noteEn: When encontrar gives a judgment, a normally marks a specific person. A writer can also use it before a thing treated as animate or personified. Ordinary inanimate things normally omit a: encuentro útil esta herramienta.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: human (a person, or a form of address)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Humano can be a noun for a human being as well as an adjective meaning ‘human.’ Used on its own while speaking to someone, it can address that person as ‘human.’

cardDefinitions.promptEs: a pesar de + situación, cosa o acción
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens despite another fact, obstacle, or action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a pesar de before the situation, thing, or action that did not prevent the result.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A pesar de works as one connector meaning ‘despite’ or ‘in spite of.’ It can be followed by a noun or by an action verb in its unchanged dictionary form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir.

example.es: Caminamos a pesar de estar cansados.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you say that you find a person or thing surprising, difficult, or another quality?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of encontrar with the target and a describing word that gives your judgment.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Encontrar here means ‘to find’ in the sense of forming a judgment, not discovering a location. The target and description can appear in either order. The description matches the target in number and, when the form allows it, gender. Use personal a before a specific person; an inanimate target normally has no a unless it is deliberately personified.

example.es: Encuentro simpática a la nueva profesora.
example.en: I find the new teacher friendly.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: A gyroscope is a spinning device whose axis resists being reoriented and can slowly turn through precession.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A rapidly spinning rotor has angular momentum, so changing the direction of its axis produces motion that can seem counterintuitive. Precession is the gradual turning of that axis under an applied force such as gravity.

regions.labelEs: A PESAR DE MIS AÑOS DE ESTUDIAR FÍSICA, TODAVÍA ENCUENTRO INQUIETANTES A LOS GIROSCOPIOS.

applications.exampleEs: A PESAR DE MIS AÑOS DE ESTUDIAR FÍSICA
applications.explanationEn: A pesar de forms the contrast connector, and the following words name the experience that did not remove the reaction.
Encuentro gives the judgment, inquietantes is plural to match los giroscopios, and a treats the gyroscopes as animate or personified targets—an effect reinforced when one later speaks.
Here a marks los giroscopios as a personified target of the judgment; ordinary inanimate targets usually omit it.
